_note: HAND-CURATED, human judgment — not derived from any filing content or heuristic. Maps each hyperscaler demand filer (by ticker) to the resource_id(s) its AI-infrastructure capex is judged relevant to. Revise deliberately; do not auto-generate. Every entry must keep a real _rationale sentence.

mappings.name: Microsoft
mappings._rationale: Azure and its OpenAI partnership drive large purchases of Nvidia AI accelerators (GPU), the HBM stacked on them, server DRAM for AI hosts, and NAND for Azure's public storage tier.

mappings.name: Alphabet/Google
mappings._rationale: Google Cloud buys Nvidia GPUs and HBM alongside its own TPUs, plus server DRAM and NAND for Cloud Storage, so its AI capex touches all four.

mappings.name: Amazon
mappings._rationale: AWS is the largest public cloud and storage provider, so its capex spans GPUs and HBM for AI instances, DRAM for compute, and heavy NAND for S3/EBS storage.

mappings.name: Meta
mappings._rationale: Meta's capex is dominated by internal AI-training GPU clusters (GPU + HBM) and their server DRAM; NAND is excluded because Meta runs no third-party public storage cloud driving separate flash demand.
